newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end on much higher note led by U.S.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end on much higher note led by U.S.

text.p: Swedish shares ended Tuesday on a much higher note, inspired by market strength in the U.S. after lower-than-expected U.S. consumer price data.
"After the U.S. figure a lot of customers entered the market again. It will continue to rise tomorrow if New York doesn't loose steam," a broker said.
Market reaction to the government budget was insignificant as copies were leaked widely in Swedish papers on Tuesday.
The Stockholm general index climbed 2.39 percent 2,665.92 in turnover of 4.08 billion crowns.
Drugs major Astra rose 14.5 crowns to 352 ahead of American competitor Merck's results due on Wednesday. Lehman Brothers lifted its recommendation on Astra to outperform from neutral.
Pharmacia & Upjohn tracked the movement and closed nine crowns higher at 273.5.
Telecom group Ericsson lifted eight to 253.5.
Bearings maker SKF dipped six crowns to 175.5 after posting a 38 percent fall in profit after financial items to 501 million crowns the first quarter of 1997.
